Sort each word under Near or Far, based on distance.

teachingCards.title: Thematic Rationale
teachingCards.content: Nearby, close, and adjacent all describe something at a short distance, with adjacent specifically meaning right next to something. Remote and distant both describe something far away, with remote often implying it's also hard to reach.

teachingCards.title: Word Meanings
teachingCards.content:
Nearby: not far away, close by
Remote: so far away that reaching it is difficult
Distant: a long way off in space or time
Adjacent: next to or adjoining something
Close: near in distance

relatedWords: Nearby: not far away, close by
Remote: so far away that reaching it is difficult
Distant: a long way off in space or time
Adjacent: next to or adjoining something
Close: near in distance

quests.instruction: Think about a town described on a map — is it right next door, or on the edge of everything? Sort into Far or Near.
quests.definition: Neighboring, local, and 'within reach' all describe something close by, easy to access. Faraway and outlying both describe distance, with outlying specifically describing areas at the edge of a region, away from the center.
quests.example: Faraway: distant, far off | Neighboring: located close by, next to | Local: belonging to a nearby, particular area | Outlying: far from the main area or center | Within reach: close enough to be accessed easily
quests.exampleSentence: Faraway: distant, far off
quests.contextSentence: Neighboring, local, and 'within reach' all describe something close by, easy to access. Faraway and outlying both describe distance, with outlying specifically describing areas at the edge of a region, away from the center.
relatedWords: Faraway: distant, far off
Neighboring: located close by, next to
Local: belonging to a nearby, particular area
Outlying: far from the main area or center
Within reach: close enough to be accessed easily
quests.nativeTip: One far word specifically describes areas at the edge of a region, away from the center.

quests.instruction: Two of these describe a relationship, not just physical distance. Sort into Near or Far.
quests.definition: 'In the vicinity' and 'close-knit' both describe closeness, with close-knit used figuratively for a tightly connected group of people. 'Long-distance', 'estranged', and 'far-flung' all describe distance, with estranged used figuratively for a relationship that's become distant or broken, and far-flung describing places spread widely apart.
quests.example: Far-flung: spread over a great distance | Long-distance: covering or involving a great distance | Estranged: no longer close, often describing a broken relationship | Close-knit: tightly and closely connected, describing a group | In the vicinity: near or close to a place
quests.exampleSentence: Far-flung: spread over a great distance
quests.contextSentence: 'In the vicinity' and 'close-knit' both describe closeness, with close-knit used figuratively for a tightly connected group of people. 'Long-distance', 'estranged', and 'far-flung' all describe distance, with estranged used figuratively for a relationship that's become distant or broken, and far-flung describing places spread widely apart.
relatedWords: Far-flung: spread over a great distance
Long-distance: covering or involving a great distance
Estranged: no longer close, often describing a broken relationship
Close-knit: tightly and closely connected, describing a group
In the vicinity: near or close to a place
quests.nativeTip: Think figuratively — about a family relationship as well as an actual location.
